item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Ghostwalk New Bern — Sat Oct 24, 6:00 PM — Historic Downtown New Bern
item.description:
Join us for Ghostwalk Oct. 22-24, 2026 from 6pm to 9pm. Now in its 36th year, Ghostwalk is a family-friendly fall event that combines spirits from New Bern's past, talented local volunteer actors, historic sites, and a fun-filled, creative environment. For three evenings in October you’ll be able to step into the time machine and visit with ghosts of lively New Bernians, famous people and ordinary folks. You’ll visit 13 “ghost sites” in Cedar Grove Cemetery and on the porches of historic homes. In keeping with this year’s theme, “Voices of Freedom, Stories from 250 Years”, you will hear stories and meet characters from all across our 250 year history.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Coping During Uncertain Times — Wed Jul 29, 12:00 PM
item.description:
People have a powerful need to understand and predict their environments in order to feel in control. When we are exposed to potential threats to our well-being, we naturally respond to this uncertainty with anxiety and fear. This training will address ways of effectively coping with uncertainty in today’s media-saturated world. The course will examine how to remain positive and functional despite the risks of living in a changing world. Included will be practical tips for coping with uncertainty, re-establishing control and how to speak to children about fear.
Click on Carolina Talent registration link and select the “Request” button to automatically enroll.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

Senora Lynch (Haliwa-Saponi)Karina McMillan (Lumbee)Harlen Chavis (Lumbee)Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba)Coda Cavalier (Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation)Amy Postoak (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians) and Johnny Postoak (Muscogee Creek) of Three Sisters DesignsRhiannon “Skye” Tafoya (Eastern Band of Cherokee and Santa Clara Pueblo)Joshua Adams (Eastern Band of Cherokee)Idalis Dial (Coharie)Tim Locklear (Lumbee)NC State students Ashtyn Thomas (Lumbee) and Victoria Wilson
